comment: Class is about the history of the American education system and is a very good option for the fys requirement. Do not need to really read any of the books or other course materials and essay assignments are not bad for a fys class.

Dr. Shields is such an amazing guy who genuinely cares about his students and their outside lives. Makes class comfortable and is basically an open discussion, and is really knowledgeable about his field which shows in his lectures. Readings are manageable and there's 3 essays which he gives advance notice on and grades fairly. Such a great FYS.

Dr. Shields is easily the kindest professor I had for my first semester- he brought candy for us every class and truly cares about our personal lives. The readings are not very necessary as long as you pay attention during the lectures, and the 3 essays are manageable as he gives you the sources ahead of time and grades fairly. Great guy and FYS!

Dr. Shields is amazing! He created a comfortable class atmosphere and you can tell he really cares about his students. Class is structured the same every day with heavily discussion-based lectures. There are daily readings but you can usually get by with only skimming (though actually doing them will help you participate in discussions).
I love Dr. Shields and will be taking more of his classes in the future! I would totally recommend him to First Years and anyone interested in trying out Leadership.

He is SO nice and understanding. Barely any homework, and you really don't need to do the reading. We have only written a couple of essays (he pushed the deadline back on both). Material is easy and interesting. The class is like a discussion. You don't have to participate and there's no cold-calling.

Our class met at noon, and he almost always brought snacks, even gluten-free ones for a classmate. He places a lot of value on participation, so discussions can take a long time. As long as you've done the reading, you should be fine. One thing is that the midterm was the first exam we had was our midterm, so none of us knew what to expect

Dr. Shields is easily the most inspiring and engaging professor I have had at Richmond. His leadership course this semester taught me so much about education in the US and current policy. I would recommend him to anyone who wants to take a class that they are truly excited about.

Dr. Shields is such a kind teacher!! He assigns a ton of reading (like every FYS) but says "if you can get to it" or "read as much as you can" (aka you don't really need to do the reading as long as you take notes in class). Education and Society is easiest FYS and he really isn't a hard grader for papers.

Dr. Shields is very passionate about his area of expertise and it shows during his lectures. He's really caring about his students and loves when you participate. Not too difficult only 4 papers all semester, fair grader, would recommend for an easy FYS
He is a great professor. He cares a lot and is very passionate about what he lectures. Ask questions- he will be honest, straight-forward, and loves to give you knowledge of hands on his experience.

Dr. Shields is one of the most inspirational professors I ever had. His lectures are pretty interesting and motivating on how can can provide better education and equal opportunities to all children. He really values participation and you are going to have to write a lot. That shouldn't stop you from taking his class though.
Dr. Shields is such a brilliant mentor. He always gives good feedback on papers and respects every student. His FYS course is the easiest and most interesting course!! Definitely will take it again!!

Great professor who's very knowledgeable and insightful. Facilitates thought-provoking discussion and makes your contributions seem so valued. Makes the class (education and society) very interesting and engaging. Respected in his field and loved by his students! He is super open and invites students to talk things out over coffee.

Professor Shields is SUCH a nice guy. He is so passionate about what he teaches. Sometimes unclear about what he wants on his papers, but is very fair with grading. Definitely strives to help his students succeed and enjoy the topic!

He is very passionate about what he is teaching. He sometimes goes off in tangents which aren't always that bad. He has a lot to say in the little time available. His tests are fair , but he does grade pretty harshly on his papers. Overall, great teacher and class. I would love to have him again as a teacher.
Amazing professor! Was not interested in the subject at all but he made the class interesting!

This guy is the man.  I totally recommend taking him.  He's really helpful on papers and will meet at any time.  He is not a hard grader and loves to see you put in good effort.  Dr. Shields, you my boy.

FYS Education and Citizenship was an interesting topic but he did not do that great a job of adding further insight beyond what the books said. very unclear with the essay topics and what is due for class. don't have to do most of the reading...but he assigns a lot of it. he is lenient and will push back deadlines and seems to care about students.

Ok, so I m currently looking for classes to add and am so sorry Dr. Shields is not teaching any of the classes I need to take. He is by far the best professor I have had at UofR. Incredibly clear, supportive, helped me a lot and I love that guy. If you can take Dr. Shields's class DON'T MISS THE SHOT!

One of the most helpful teachers in Jepson School. Students clearly expect to get out of the classroom and know how to become leaders- that aint possible. Dr. Shields will teach you certainly most important concepts and will explain them in detail and clearly- If you read the assignments, you shall have no problem!TAKE THE CLASS- its absolutely gre
Shields rocks! Loved the class - def recommend it. how he allows for conversation and really pushes with good ideas. Great selection of readings.

Professor Shields means well but has trouble executing his meaningful agenda for the class. He can be hilarious and make the class interesting but don't be surprised to be bored because he just lets people go on and on. The class is only fun if everybody reads the material. Shields is a nice guy but I wish he would take it more seriously.
No preperation for classes, very very detail orientated tests (learn the lists), abysmal teacher no help, and had no time for his students, never retured work, Dont take him if you can avoid him!
Shields is a nice guy that is very easy to be around. However, he does not always explain the subject in the best way and makes it hard to get an A in the class. Overall, he is still a good teacher.
No Comments
Dr. Shields is great. Very engaging. He assigns too much work...but I'm glad I took his class.

Dr. Shields is one of the best teachers at Jepson. He is clearly one of the more well-rounded teachers I have ever had at UofR. He provides a comfortable learning environment while at the same time challenging all of students to excel.
No Comments
Shields is by far the most attractive professor on campus.  Who cares how his class is, you can stare at him for 50 minutes and not get bored!

i learned next to nothing from this man. he came to class with sparknotes each day to guide discussions. mabe it was just because he was a new prof, but i honestly thought i was smarter than him. he is a VERY nice man though, and not bad on the eyes.
Nice guy and good teacher who is very willing to help you out.  You'll understand the readings when he explains them, and he facilitates good discussion.  Make sure you participate.

He assigns a lot of reading but always follows it up with discussion. Reading not always necessary. His midterm is more detail oriented than expected. He likes political science. Some lessons relate to politics. It's hard to get a read off of him. You don't know if your comments were sufficent.
